## Analysis

**What the task_score actually is:** for every candidate, `task_score` tracks the raw forward velocity (m/s) almost exactly (C1: `forward_speed` 5.85 vs `task_score` 5.83). So the metric is "how fast is the ant's torso moving along +x at iteration N" — the reward *scale* is irrelevant, only the **gradient of the reward w.r.t. speed** matters for continued progress.

**Gradient budget at current speeds (~6–7 m/s):**

| | speed-term gradient (dR/dv) | posture/regularizer drag |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | ~1.0 (linear vx) | strong: 0.5·up_z (linear tilt), height target 0.5 m, 1e-4·Σdof_vel² (penalizes fast leg swing = the speed mechanism) |
| C2 | ~0.10 (tanh/10 + high-speed bonus) | mild (only penalizes up_z<0.4) |
| C3 | ~0.7 (0.2·v + Gaussian tracking @9 m/s, σ=3.5) | mild hinge tilt/lateral + fall penalty, alive bonus |
| C4 | ~0.24 (0.2·v + 0.6·tanh(v/6)) | soft quadratic tilt, mild regs |

**Why C3 wins.** It is the only candidate whose reward keeps a *strong, well-placed* gradient exactly in the 6–9 m/s band (the Gaussian tracking term peaks its gradient near 6.5–7 m/s and is still positive up to ~11 m/s), while its stabilizing terms are hinge-based (only bite past thresholds) so they don't fight the speed objective. It also has a genuine fall penalty + alive bonus, so the extra speed isn't bought with tumbling. Empirically it is already far ahead and still climbing fastest (Δ≈0.31/50 iters vs ≈0.22–0.24 for the others), and its slow-growing `speed_tracking` component (0.03→1.46) confirms the policy is still being pulled upward toward its 9 m/s target.

**Why the others lose.** C4 has the right structure (unsaturated linear term) but a 5× weaker speed gradient and its tanh is already flat, so it creeps toward a lower plateau. C1's 1.0·vx is tempting, but its linear upright term, height preference and joint-velocity penalty directly tax the leaning/fast-leg gait needed for speed — it already shows the flattest recent growth despite the biggest nominal gradient. C2 is worst: with tanh/10 and a tiny saturating high-speed bonus, its gradient at 6 m/s is ~0.1, its log has just gone flat (6.16→6.16), and with no alive bonus/fall term it is exposed to the dive-and-tumble exploit that caps forward progress.

**Prediction at 3,000 iters:** C3 ≈ 10–12 m/s, C4 ≈ 9–10, C1 ≈ 8–9, C2 ≈ 7–8.
